definition: Publicize means to make something widely known to the public.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word publicize. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know publicize should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The trick isn't building the night market — it's publicizing it until three neighborhoods can't imagine Friday without it.
Announce is a single act — one statement, one audience, done — where to publicize is to keep spreading the word until the public at large has heard.
Trumpet goes further than publicize — the spreading turns boastful, volume standing in for information.

To promote something is to push it toward success — ticket sales, votes, a career — with public awareness only a means to that end. Publicize stops at the awareness itself: make the thing widely known and the job is done, whatever happens next.

Broadcast implies the airwaves — one sender scattering the message wide in a single transmission. Publicize is indifferent to the channel: posters, calendar listings, a reporter's favor all count, and the spreading can take months. Broadcast names a method; publicize names only the goal.

Six months of steady noise later — star parties in the calendar listings, a comet named on the local news — the fund closed out.
Publicize is the working verb because it means to make something widely known to the public — the telescope was always there; the town's awareness wasn't.
Advertise usually means buying the attention; publicize covers every way of earning it, paid or not.
Publicize is the plain workhorse for making things widely known, and its plainness is the point: it doesn't say how.
